about: The epistola of the formulary “Sunday after the Ascension” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

s01.translation: Dearly beloved: Be prudent and keep watch in prayer. But above all, maintain constant love for one another, for love covers a multitude of sins. Be hospitable to one another without grumbling. As each of you has received a gift, use it to serve one another as good stewards of God’s manifold grace. If anyone speaks, let him speak as one who speaks the words of God; if anyone serves, let him do so as one relying on the strength God supplies, so that in all things God may be honored through Jesus Christ our Lord.

alignments.gloss: maintain constant love for one another
use it to serve one another
let him speak as one who speaks the words of God
let him do so as one relying on the strength

w016.explanation: The participle describes the faithful Peter addresses: they are to keep a mutual and constant charity. The sentence has no verb in the second person, and no separate word expresses its subject, an understood you.

w022.explanation: The adjective is the predicate of an understood subject, the faithful Peter addresses. The Latin leaves out both the subject and the verb: “[be] hospitable to one another”.

w029.explanation: Here the grace received by each person is to be used in serving the others. The rendering “a gift” makes this bestowed-gift sense explicit. The later “grace of God” describes its manifold divine source, not a different Latin lemma.

w033.explanation: The plural participle describes the faithful, although the singular “unusquísque” comes before it: each is to minister to the others the grace received. No separate word expresses its subject.

w043.note: After the conditional clauses, Latin leaves the repeated predicates implicit. The captions for “quasi sermones Dei” and “tamquam ex virtute” supply them to preserve the exhortation and comparisons.
